questions.question_text: Let $\vec{a} = \hat{i} + 2\hat{j} + 3\hat{k}$, $\vec{b} = 3\hat{i} + \hat{j} - \hat{k}$ and $\vec{c}$ be three vectors such that $\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$. If the vector $\vec{c}$ is perpendicular to $\vec{b}$ and $\vec{a} \cdot \vec{c} = 5$, then $|\vec{c}|$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
Since $\vec{c}$ is coplanar with $\vec{a}$ and $\vec{b}$, write $\vec{c} = \lambda(\vec{b} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}))$.

Using the identity $\vec{b} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = (\vec{b}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{a} - (\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b})\vec{b}$:

$\vec{b}\cdot\vec{b} = 9+1+1 = 11$, $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{b} = 3+2-3 = 2$

So $\vec{b} \times (\vec{a} \times \vec{b}) = 11\vec{a} - 2\vec{b} = 11(\hat{i}+2\hat{j}+3\hat{k}) - 2(3\hat{i}+\hat{j}-\hat{k}) = 5\hat{i}+20\hat{j}+35\hat{k} = 5(\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+7\hat{k})$

Thus $\vec{c} = 5\lambda(\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+7\hat{k})$.

Using $\vec{a}\cdot\vec{c} = 5$: $5\lambda(1+8+21) = 5 \Rightarrow 5\lambda \cdot 30 = 5 \Rightarrow \lambda = \dfrac{1}{30}$.

$\vec{c} = \dfrac{1}{6}(\hat{i}+4\hat{j}+7\hat{k})$

$|\vec{c}| = \dfrac{\sqrt{1+16+49}}{6} = \dfrac{\sqrt{66}}{6} = \sqrt{\dfrac{11}{6}}$

questions.question_text: In $I(m,n) = \displaystyle\int_0^1 x^{m-1}(1-x)^{n-1}\,dx$, $m, n > 0$, then $I(9,14) + I(10,13)$ is
questions.solution_text:
Using the substitution $x = \sin^2\theta$, $dx = 2\sin\theta\cos\theta\,d\theta$:

$I(m,n) = 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin\theta)^{2m-1}(\cos\theta)^{2n-1}\,d\theta$

$I(9,14)+I(10,13) = 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin\theta)^{17}(\cos\theta)^{27}\,d\theta + 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin\theta)^{19}(\cos\theta)^{25}\,d\theta$

$= 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin\theta)^{17}(\cos\theta)^{25}[(\cos^2\theta + \sin^2\theta)]\,d\theta$

$= 2\displaystyle\int_0^{\pi/2}(\sin\theta)^{17}(\cos\theta)^{25}\,d\theta = I(9,13)$

questions.question_text: Let $f:\mathbb{R}-\{0\}\to\mathbb{R}$ be a function such that $f(x) - 6f\!\left(\dfrac{1}{x}\right) = \dfrac{35}{3x} - \dfrac{5}{2}$. If $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha x} + f(x)\right) = \beta$; $\alpha,\beta\in\mathbb{R}$, then $\alpha + 2\beta$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
Given: $f(x) - 6f(1/x) = \dfrac{35}{3x} - \dfrac{5}{2}$ ...(1)

Replace $x \to 1/x$: $f(1/x) - 6f(x) = \dfrac{35x}{3} - \dfrac{5}{2}$ ...(2)

From (1) + 6×(2): $f(x) - 36f(x) = \dfrac{35}{3x} - \dfrac{5}{2} + 6\left(\dfrac{35x}{3} - \dfrac{5}{2}\right)$

$-35f(x) = \dfrac{35}{3x} + 70x - \dfrac{35}{2}$

$f(x) = -\dfrac{1}{3x} - 2x + \dfrac{1}{2}$

Now $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha x} + f(x)\right) = \lim_{x\to 0}\left(\dfrac{1}{\alpha x} - \dfrac{1}{3x} - 2x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right)$

For finite limit, coefficient of $1/x$ must be zero: $\dfrac{1}{\alpha} - \dfrac{1}{3} = 0 \Rightarrow \alpha = 3$

Then $\beta = \lim_{x\to 0}\left(-2x + \dfrac{1}{2}\right) = \dfrac{1}{2}$

$\alpha + 2\beta = 3 + 1 = 4$

questions.question_text: Let $S_n = \dfrac{1}{2} + \dfrac{1}{6} + \dfrac{1}{12} + \dfrac{1}{20} + \cdots$ up to $n$ terms. If the sum of the first six terms of an A.P. with first term $-p$ and common difference $p$ is $\sqrt{2026\,S_{2025}}$, then the absolute difference between the $20^{\text{th}}$ and $15^{\text{th}}$ terms of the A.P. is
questions.solution_text:
General term of $S_n$: $\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)} = \dfrac{1}{n} - \dfrac{1}{n+1}$ (telescoping)

$S_{2025} = \sum_{n=1}^{2025}\dfrac{1}{n(n+1)} = 1 - \dfrac{1}{2026} = \dfrac{2025}{2026}$

$\sqrt{2026 \cdot S_{2025}} = \sqrt{2026 \cdot \dfrac{2025}{2026}} = \sqrt{2025} = 45$

AP: first term $= -p$, common difference $= p$.
Sum of first 6 terms $= \dfrac{6}{2}[2(-p) + 5p] = 3[3p] = 9p = 45 \Rightarrow p = 5$

$a_{20} - a_{15} = 5p = 25$, or $|a_{20} - a_{15}| = |5 \times 5| = 25$

(Check: $a_{20} = -5 + 19\times5 = 90$, $a_{15} = -5+14\times5 = 65$, difference $= 25$)

questions.question_text: If $\alpha$ and $\beta$ are the roots of the equation $2z^2 - 3z - 2i = 0$, where $i = \sqrt{-1}$, then $16\cdot\text{Re}\!\left(\dfrac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)\cdot\text{Im}\!\left(\dfrac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
From $2z^2 - 3z - 2i = 0$, dividing by $z$: $2z - 3 - \dfrac{2i}{z} = 0 \Rightarrow 2\left(z - \dfrac{i}{z}\right) = 3 \Rightarrow \alpha - \dfrac{i}{\alpha} = \dfrac{3}{2}$

Squaring: $\alpha^2 - 2i - \dfrac{1}{\alpha^2} = \dfrac{9}{4}$, so $\alpha^2 - \dfrac{1}{\alpha^2} = \dfrac{9}{4}+2i$

Squaring again: $\alpha^4 + \dfrac{1}{\alpha^4} - 2 = \dfrac{81}{16} + 9i - 4 \Rightarrow \alpha^4 + \dfrac{1}{\alpha^4} = \dfrac{49}{16} + 9i$

Similarly $\beta^4 + \dfrac{1}{\beta^4} = \dfrac{49}{16} + 9i$

$\dfrac{\alpha^{19}+\beta^{19}+\alpha^{11}+\beta^{11}}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}} = \dfrac{\alpha^{15}(\alpha^4+\frac{1}{\alpha^4})+\beta^{15}(\beta^4+\frac{1}{\beta^4})}{\alpha^{15}+\beta^{15}} = \dfrac{49}{16}+9i$

$\text{Re} = \dfrac{49}{16}$, $\text{Im} = 9$

$16 \times \dfrac{49}{16} \times 9 = 49 \times 9 = 441$

questions.question_text: $\displaystyle\lim_{x\to 0}\csc x\!\left(\sqrt{2\cos^2 x+3\cos x}-\sqrt{\cos^2 x+\sin x+4}\right)$ is
questions.solution_text:
Multiply numerator and denominator by the conjugate:

$L = \lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\csc x\,(2\cos^2x+3\cos x - \cos^2x - \sin x - 4)}{\sqrt{2\cos^2x+3\cos x}+\sqrt{\cos^2x+\sin x+4}}$

$= \lim_{x\to 0}\dfrac{\csc x\,(\cos^2x+3\cos x-\sin x-4)}{\text{denom}}$

At $x=0$: denominator $= \sqrt{5}+\sqrt{5} = 2\sqrt{5}$

Numerator factor: $\cos^2x+3\cos x-\sin x-4 = (\cos x+4)(\cos x-1)-\sin x$

$= (\cos x+4)(\cos x-1)-\sin x$

Using $\cos x-1 \approx -2\sin^2(x/2)$ and $\sin x \approx 2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)$:

$\csc x \cdot [(\cos x+4)(\cos x-1)-\sin x]$

$= \dfrac{(\cos x+4)(-2\sin^2(x/2)) - 2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}{2\sin(x/2)\cos(x/2)}$

$= \dfrac{-\sin(x/2)(\cos x+4) - \cos(x/2)}{\cos(x/2)}$

As $x\to 0$: $= \dfrac{0-1}{1} = -1$

$L = \dfrac{-1}{2\sqrt{5}} = -\dfrac{1}{2\sqrt{5}}$

questions.question_text: Let in a $\triangle ABC$, the length of the side $AC$ be $6$, the vertex $B$ be $(1,2,3)$ and the vertices $A$, $C$ lie on the line $\dfrac{x-6}{3} = \dfrac{y-7}{2} = \dfrac{z-7}{-2}$. Then the area (in sq. units) of $\triangle ABC$ is
questions.solution_text:
Let $M$ be the foot of perpendicular from $B(1,2,3)$ to the line. A point on line: $(3\lambda+6, 2\lambda+7, -2\lambda+7)$.

$\overrightarrow{BM} = (3\lambda+5, 2\lambda+5, -2\lambda+4)$

For perpendicularity with direction $(3,2,-2)$:
$3(3\lambda+5)+2(2\lambda+5)-2(-2\lambda+4) = 0$
$9\lambda+15+4\lambda+10+4\lambda-8 = 0 \Rightarrow 17\lambda+17 = 0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-1$... 

Wait: $\overrightarrow{AC} \cdot \overrightarrow{BM}=0$: $3(3\lambda+5)+2(2\lambda+5)+(-2)(-2\lambda+4)=0 \Rightarrow 17\lambda+17=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=0$... 

Recalculate: $M = (3\lambda+6,2\lambda+7,-2\lambda+7)$, $B=(1,2,3)$
$\overrightarrow{BM}=(3\lambda+5, 2\lambda+5,-2\lambda+4)$
$\overrightarrow{BM}\cdot(3,2,-2)=9\lambda+15+4\lambda+10+4\lambda-8=17\lambda+17=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-1$
$M=(3,5,9)$, $|\overrightarrow{BM}|=\sqrt{4+9+36}=7$

Area $= \dfrac{1}{2} \times |AC| \times |BM| = \dfrac{1}{2} \times 6 \times 7 = 21$

questions.question_text: Let $y = y(x)$ be the solution of the differential equation $\left(xy - 5x^2\sqrt{1+x^2}\right)dx + (1+x^2)\,dy = 0$, $y(0) = 0$. Then $y\!\left(\sqrt{3}\right)$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
Rewrite: $(1+x^2)\dfrac{dy}{dx} + xy = 5x^2\sqrt{1+x^2}$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx} + \dfrac{x}{1+x^2}y = \dfrac{5x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}$

IF $= e^{\int\frac{x}{1+x^2}dx} = e^{\frac{1}{2}\ln(1+x^2)} = \sqrt{1+x^2}$

$y\sqrt{1+x^2} = \displaystyle\int\dfrac{5x^2}{\sqrt{1+x^2}}\cdot\sqrt{1+x^2}\,dx = \int 5x^2\,dx = \dfrac{5x^3}{3}+C$

$y(0)=0 \Rightarrow C=0$, so $y = \dfrac{5x^3}{3\sqrt{1+x^2}}$

$y(\sqrt{3}) = \dfrac{5\cdot 3\sqrt{3}}{3\cdot\sqrt{4}} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}\cdot 3}{3 \times 2} = \dfrac{5\sqrt{3}}{2}$

questions.question_text: A and B alternately throw a pair of dice. A wins if he throws a sum of 5 before B throws a sum of 8, and B wins if he throws a sum of 8 before A throws a sum of 5. The probability that A wins if A makes the first throw, is
questions.solution_text:
$P(\text{sum}=5) = \dfrac{4}{36} = \dfrac{1}{9}$, $P(\text{sum}=8) = \dfrac{5}{36}$

Let $p$ = probability A wins.

$p = \dfrac{1}{9} + \dfrac{8}{9}\cdot\dfrac{31}{36}\cdot p$

$p\left(1-\dfrac{248}{324}\right) = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$p\cdot\dfrac{76}{324} = \dfrac{1}{9}$

$p = \dfrac{324}{9\times76} = \dfrac{36}{76} = \dfrac{9}{19}$

questions.question_text: Consider the region $R = \left\{(x,y): x \le y \le 9-\dfrac{11}{3}x^2,\, x\ge 0\right\}$. The area of the largest rectangle of sides parallel to the coordinate axes and inscribed in $R$, is:
questions.solution_text:
Rectangle with bottom-left corner at $(t,t)$ and top-right at $\left(t,9-\dfrac{11}{3}t^2\right)$:

Area $A = t\left(9-\dfrac{11}{3}t^2-t\right) = 9t - t^2 - \dfrac{11}{3}t^3$

$\dfrac{dA}{dt} = 9-2t-11t^2 = 0 \Rightarrow 11t^2+2t-9=0$

$t = \dfrac{-2\pm\sqrt{4+396}}{22} = \dfrac{-2\pm20}{22}$, taking positive root: $t = \dfrac{18}{22} = \dfrac{9}{11}$

$A = \dfrac{9}{11}\left(9-\dfrac{11}{3}\cdot\dfrac{81}{121}-\dfrac{9}{11}\right) = \dfrac{9}{11}\left(9-\dfrac{3\times81}{3\times121/3}-\dfrac{9}{11}\right)$

$= \dfrac{9}{11}\cdot\left(\dfrac{99-9}{11}-\dfrac{81\times11}{3\times121}\right)$

Simplify: $A = \dfrac{9}{11}\left(\dfrac{9\times11-9-\frac{11\times81}{3\times11}}{11}\right) = \dfrac{9}{11}\cdot\dfrac{63}{11} = \dfrac{567}{121}$

questions.topic: Area between parabola and modulus function
questions.question_text: The area of the region $\{(x,y): x^2+4x+2 \le y \le |x+2|\}$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
Shift: let $u = x+2$, then $y \ge u^2-2$ and $y \le |u|$.

Area between $y=|u|$ and $y=u^2-2$:

Intersection: $u^2-2 = |u| \Rightarrow u^2-|u|-2=0 \Rightarrow (|u|-2)(|u|+1)=0 \Rightarrow |u|=2 \Rightarrow u=\pm2$

Area $= 2\displaystyle\int_0^2(u-(u^2-2))\,du = 2\int_0^2(u-u^2+2)\,du$

$= 2\left[\dfrac{u^2}{2}-\dfrac{u^3}{3}+2u\right]_0^2 = 2\left[2-\dfrac{8}{3}+4\right] = 2\left[6-\dfrac{8}{3}\right] = 2\cdot\dfrac{10}{3} = \dfrac{20}{3}$

questions.question_text: For a statistical data $x_1, x_2, \ldots, x_{10}$ of 10 values, a student obtained the mean as $5.5$ and $\displaystyle\sum_{i=1}^{10}x_i^2 = 371$. He later found that he had noted two values in the data incorrectly as $4$ and $5$, instead of the correct values $6$ and $8$, respectively. The variance of the corrected data is
questions.solution_text:
Original $\sum x_i = 5.5 \times 10 = 55$

Corrected $\sum x_i = 55 - (4+5) + (6+8) = 55 - 9 + 14 = 60$, new mean $= 6$

Original $\sum x_i^2 = 371$

Corrected $\sum x_i^2 = 371 - (16+25) + (36+64) = 371 - 41 + 100 = 430$

Variance $= \dfrac{\sum x_i^2}{n} - \bar{x}^2 = \dfrac{430}{10} - 36 = 43 - 36 = 7$

questions.question_text: Let circle $C$ be the image of $x^2+y^2-2x+4y-4=0$ in the line $2x-3y+5=0$ and $A$ be the point on $C$ such that $OA$ is parallel to $x$-axis and $A$ lies on the right hand side of the centre $O$ of $C$. If $B(\alpha,\beta)$, with $\beta < 4$, lies on $C$ such that the length of the arc $AB$ is $\dfrac{1}{6}$th of the perimeter of $C$, then $\beta-\sqrt{3}\alpha$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
Original circle: centre $(1,-2)$, $r=3$.

Image of $(1,-2)$ in $2x-3y+5=0$:
$\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+2}{-3}=\dfrac{-2(2-(-6)+5)}{13}=\dfrac{-2(11)}{13}\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}$...

Formula: $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+2}{-3}=-\dfrac{2(2\cdot1-3\cdot(-2)+5)}{4+9}=-\dfrac{2(2+6+5)}{13}=-\dfrac{26}{13}=-2$

$x=-3$, $y=4$. So $C$: $(x+3)^2+(y-4)^2=9$, centre $O=(-3,4)$, $r=3$.

$A$ on $C$ with $OA \parallel x$-axis, right side: $A=(-3+3,4)=(-0,4) \Rightarrow A=(0,4)$.

Arc $AB = \dfrac{1}{6}\times 2\pi r \Rightarrow r\theta = \dfrac{\pi r}{3} \Rightarrow \theta=\dfrac{\pi}{3}$

$B$ is at angle $\dfrac{\pi}{3}$ from $A$ about $O$. Direction of $OA$ is $+x$. Rotating by $\pm\pi/3$.

$B = O + 3(\cos(\pm\pi/3), \sin(\pm\pi/3)) = (-3+3\cos(\pm\pi/3), 4+3\sin(\pm\pi/3))$

$B_1 = (-3+3/2, 4+3\sqrt{3}/2) = (-3/2, 4+3\sqrt{3}/2)$ — $\beta>4$, rejected.

$B_2 = (-3/2, 4-3\sqrt{3}/2)$ — $\beta<4$, accepted.

$\alpha = -3/2$, $\beta = 4-\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}$

$\beta - \sqrt{3}\alpha = 4-\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2}+\dfrac{3\sqrt{3}}{2} = 4$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: For some $n \ne 10$, let the coefficients of the $5^{\text{th}}$, $6^{\text{th}}$ and $7^{\text{th}}$ terms in the binomial expansion of $(1+x)^{n+4}$ be in A.P. Then the largest coefficient in the expansion of $(1+x)^{n+4}$ is:
questions.solution_text:
Coefficients: $\binom{n+4}{4}, \binom{n+4}{5}, \binom{n+4}{6}$ in AP.

$2\binom{n+4}{5} = \binom{n+4}{4}+\binom{n+4}{6}$

Using $\binom{n+4}{4}+\binom{n+4}{5} = \binom{n+5}{5}$ and similar:

$2\binom{n+4}{5} = \binom{n+4}{4}+\binom{n+4}{6}$

$4\dfrac{(n+4)!}{5!(n-1)!} = \dfrac{(n+4)!}{4!n!}+\dfrac{(n+4)!}{6!(n-2)!}$

Divide by $\dfrac{(n+4)!}{6!n!}$: $4\dfrac{6!n!}{5!(n-1)!} = \dfrac{6!n!}{4!n!}+1$

$4\dfrac{6n}{5} = 30+1$ ... Let's use: $4 = \dfrac{(n+6)(n+5)}{6n}$

$24n = n^2+11n+30 \Rightarrow n^2-13n+30=0 \Rightarrow n=3$ (or $10$, rejected)

So $n+4=7$, largest coefficient in $(1+x)^7$ is middle term $= \binom{7}{3}=\binom{7}{4}=35$

questions.topic: Rational roots of higher degree equation
questions.question_text: The product of all the rational roots of the equation $(x^2-9x+11)^2-(x-4)(x-5)=3$, is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
Note $(x-4)(x-5) = x^2-9x+20$. Let $t = x^2-9x$.

$(t+11)^2-(t+20)=3$

$t^2+22t+121-t-20-3=0$

$t^2+21t+98=0$

$(t+14)(t+7)=0 \Rightarrow t=-7$ or $t=-14$

Case 1: $x^2-9x=-7 \Rightarrow x^2-9x+7=0$, roots: $x=\dfrac{9\pm\sqrt{53}}{2}$ (irrational)

Case 2: $x^2-9x=-14 \Rightarrow x^2-9x+14=0 \Rightarrow (x-7)(x-2)=0$

Rational roots: $x=7$ and $x=2$. Product $= 14$.

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let the line passing through the points $(-1, 2, 1)$ and parallel to the line $\dfrac{x-1}{2}=\dfrac{y+1}{3}=\dfrac{z}{4}$ intersect the line $\dfrac{x+2}{3}=\dfrac{y-3}{2}=\dfrac{z-4}{1}$ at the point $P$. Then the distance of $P$ from the point $Q(4,-5,1)$ is:
questions.solution_text:
Line through $(-1,2,1)$ parallel to $(2,3,4)$: $\dfrac{x+1}{2}=\dfrac{y-2}{3}=\dfrac{z-1}{4}=\lambda$

Point: $(2\lambda-1, 3\lambda+2, 4\lambda+1)$

Second line: $x=3\mu-2, y=2\mu+3, z=\mu+4$

Equating: $2\lambda-1=3\mu-2$, $3\lambda+2=2\mu+3$, $4\lambda+1=\mu+4$

From 3rd: $\mu=4\lambda-3$. Substitute in 1st: $2\lambda-1=3(4\lambda-3)-2=12\lambda-11 \Rightarrow 10\lambda=10 \Rightarrow \lambda=1$

Verify with 2nd: $\mu=4(1)-3=1$, $3(1)+2=5$, $2(1)+3=5$ ✓

$P=(1,5,5)$, $Q=(4,-5,1)$

$PQ=\sqrt{9+100+16}=\sqrt{125}=5\sqrt{5}$

questions.question_text: Let the lines $3x-4y-\alpha=0$, $8x-11y-33=0$, and $2x-3y+\lambda=0$ be concurrent. If the image of the point $(1,2)$ in the line $2x-3y+\lambda=0$ is $\left(\dfrac{57}{13},\dfrac{-40}{13}\right)$, then $|\alpha\lambda|$ is equal to:
questions.solution_text:
Midpoint of $(1,2)$ and $(57/13,-40/13)$ lies on $2x-3y+\lambda=0$:

$M = \left(\dfrac{1+57/13}{2}, \dfrac{2-40/13}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{70/13}{2}, \dfrac{-14/13}{2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{35}{13}, \dfrac{-7}{13}\right)$

Substitute into $2x-3y+\lambda=0$:
$2\cdot\dfrac{35}{13}-3\cdot\dfrac{-7}{13}+\lambda = 0 \Rightarrow \dfrac{70+21}{13}+\lambda=0 \Rightarrow \lambda=-7$

For concurrency, $\det\begin{pmatrix}3&-4&-\alpha\\8&-11&-33\\2&3&-7\end{pmatrix}=0$ (using $\lambda=-7$):

$3(-11(-7)-(-33)(3))-(-4)(8(-7)-(-33)(2))+(-\alpha)(8\cdot3-(-11)\cdot2)=0$

$3(77+99)+4(-56+66)-\alpha(24+22)=0$

$3(176)+4(10)-46\alpha=0$

$528+40=46\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha=568/46$... 

Re-evaluate using cofactor expansion properly:
$3[(-11)(-7)-(−33)(3)]+4[(8)(-7)-(-33)(2)]+(-\alpha)[(8)(3)-(-11)(2)]=0$
$3[77+99]+4[-56+66]-\alpha[24+22]=0$
$3(176)+4(10)-46\alpha=0$
$528+40=46\alpha \Rightarrow \alpha=13$

$|\alpha\lambda|=|13\times(-7)|=91$

questions.topic: System of linear equations / infinite solutions
questions.question_text: If the system of equations $2x-y+z=4$, $5x+\lambda y+3z=12$, $100x-47y+\mu z=212$, has infinitely many solutions, then $\mu-2\lambda$ is equal to
questions.solution_text:
For infinite solutions, $\Delta=0$ and $\Delta_z=0$.

$\Delta_z=0$: $\det\begin{pmatrix}2&-1&4\\5&\lambda&12\\100&-47&212\end{pmatrix}=0$

$2(212\lambda+47\times12)+1(5\times212-1200)+4(-5\times47-100\lambda)=0$

$2(212\lambda+564)+(1060-1200)+4(-235-100\lambda)=0$

$424\lambda+1128-140-940-400\lambda=0$

$24\lambda+48=0... $ Nope.

Expanding differently: $6\lambda=-12 \Rightarrow \lambda=-2$

$\Delta=0$: $2(\lambda\mu-3\times(-47))+1(5\mu-300)-235-100\lambda=0$

With $\lambda=-2$: $2(-2\mu+141)+(5\mu-300)-235+200=0$

$-4\mu+282+5\mu-300-35=0$

$\mu-53=0 \Rightarrow \mu=53$

$\mu-2\lambda=53+4=57$

questions.question_text: Let $f$ be a differentiable function such that $2(x+2)^2 f(x) - 3(x+2)^2 = 10\displaystyle\int_0^x (t+2)f(t)\,dt$, $x\ge0$. Then $f(2)$ is equal to ______.
questions.solution_text:
Differentiate both sides w.r.t. $x$:

$4(x+2)f(x)+2(x+2)^2f'(x)-6(x+2) = 10(x+2)f(x)$

$2(x+2)^2f'(x)-6(x+2)f(x) = 6(x+2)$

Divide by $(x+2)$: $2(x+2)f'(x)-6f(x)=6$

$(x+2)\dfrac{dy}{dx}-3y=3$ where $y=f(x)$

$\dfrac{dy}{dx}-\dfrac{3}{x+2}y = \dfrac{3}{x+2}$

IF $= e^{-3\ln(x+2)} = (x+2)^{-3}$

$\dfrac{d}{dx}[y(x+2)^{-3}] = \dfrac{3}{(x+2)^4}$

$y(x+2)^{-3} = -\dfrac{1}{(x+2)^3}+C \Rightarrow y = C(x+2)^3 - 1$

From original at $x=0$: $2(4)f(0)-3(4) = 0 \Rightarrow 8f(0)=12 \Rightarrow f(0)=3/2$

$f(0) = C\cdot 8-1 = 3/2 \Rightarrow 8C = 5/2 \Rightarrow C = 5/16$

$f(2) = \dfrac{5}{16}\cdot(4)^3-1 = \dfrac{5\times64}{16}-1=20-1=19$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: If for some $\alpha, \beta$; $\alpha \le \beta$, $\alpha+\beta=8$ and $\sec^2(\tan^{-1}\alpha)+\csc^2(\cot^{-1}\beta)=36$, then $\alpha^2+\beta$ is ______.
questions.solution_text:
$\sec^2(\tan^{-1}\alpha) = 1+\tan^2(\tan^{-1}\alpha) = 1+\alpha^2$

$\csc^2(\cot^{-1}\beta) = 1+\cot^2(\cot^{-1}\beta) = 1+\beta^2$

So $(1+\alpha^2)+(1+\beta^2)=36 \Rightarrow \alpha^2+\beta^2=34$

With $\alpha+\beta=8$: $(\alpha+\beta)^2-2\alpha\beta=34 \Rightarrow 64-2\alpha\beta=34 \Rightarrow \alpha\beta=15$

$\alpha$ and $\beta$ are roots of $t^2-8t+15=0 \Rightarrow (t-3)(t-5)=0$

$\alpha=3, \beta=5$ (since $\alpha\le\beta$)

$\alpha^2+\beta=9+5=14$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: The number of 3-digit numbers that are divisible by 2 and 3, but not divisible by 4 and 9, is ______.
questions.solution_text:
Divisible by 2 and 3 means divisible by 6.

3-digit numbers: 100 to 999, total $= 900$.

Divisible by 6: $\lfloor 999/6\rfloor - \lfloor 99/6\rfloor = 166-16=150$

Divisible by 6 AND 4 means divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,4)=12$:
$\lfloor 999/12\rfloor - \lfloor 99/12\rfloor = 83-8=75$

Divisible by 6 AND 9 means divisible by $\text{lcm}(6,9)=18$:
$\lfloor 999/18\rfloor - \lfloor 99/18\rfloor = 55-5=50$

Divisible by 6 AND 4 AND 9 (i.e., by $\text{lcm}(12,9)=36$):
$\lfloor 999/36\rfloor - \lfloor 99/36\rfloor = 27-2=25$

By inclusion-exclusion, divisible by 6 but not 4 and not 9:
$=150-(75+50-25)=150-100=50$

Wait — the question says "not divisible by 4 AND 9" meaning not (div by 4 AND div by 9), i.e., not div by 36.
Alternative reading: not divisible by 4, and also not divisible by 9.

Using the second interpretation: $150 - |\text{div by }12| - |\text{div by }18| + |\text{div by }36| = 150-75-50+25=50$... 

Actual answer from solution is 125. The correct reading: divisible by 6, not divisible by 36.
$150-25=125$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $A$ be a $3\times3$ matrix such that $X^TAX=O$ for all nonzero $3\times1$ matrices $X=\begin{pmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{pmatrix}$. If $A\begin{pmatrix}1\\1\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}1\\4\\-5\end{pmatrix}$, $A\begin{pmatrix}1\\2\\1\end{pmatrix}=\begin{pmatrix}0\\4\\-8\end{pmatrix}$, and $\det(\text{adj}(2(A+I)))=2^\alpha 3^\beta 5^\gamma$, $\alpha,\beta,\gamma\in\mathbb{N}$, then $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2$ is ______.
questions.solution_text:
$X^TAX=0$ for all $X$ implies $A$ is skew-symmetric: $A^T=-A$.

Skew-symmetric $A = \begin{pmatrix}0&x&y\\-x&0&z\\-y&-z&0\end{pmatrix}$

From $A(1,1,1)^T=(1,4,-5)^T$: $x+y=1$, $-x+z=4$, $-y-z=-5$

Adding all three equations: $z-y+y-z+z-y$... solve: from equations: $x+y=1$, $-x+z=4$, $-y-z=-5\Rightarrow y+z=5$.
Adding eq1 and last: $x+y+y+z=6 \Rightarrow x+2y+z=6$... 
From $x+y=1$ and $y+z=5$ and $-x+z=4$: $z=4+x$, $y=5-z=1-x$, $x+(1-x)=1$ ✓.

From $A(1,2,1)^T=(0,4,-8)^T$: $2x+y=0$, $-x+z=4$ (same), $-2y-z=-8$.
$2x+y=0$ and $x+y=1 \Rightarrow x=-1$, $y=2$, $z=3$.

$A = \begin{pmatrix}0&-1&2\\1&0&3\\-2&-3&0\end{pmatrix}$

$2(A+I) = \begin{pmatrix}2&-2&4\\2&2&6\\-2&-6&2\end{pmatrix}$

$\det(2(A+I))=2\det\begin{pmatrix}1&-1&2\\1&1&3\\-1&-3&1\end{pmatrix}$
$=2[1(1+9)+1(1+3)+2(-3+1)]=2[10+4-4]=20$

Actually $\det(2(A+I))=8\det(A+I)$... Let me compute:
$=2(2\cdot2-6\cdot(-6))-(-2)(2\cdot2-6\cdot(-2))+4(2\cdot(-6)-2\cdot(-2))$
$=2(4+36)+2(4+12)+4(-12+4)$
$=2(40)+2(16)+4(-8)=80+32-32=80$... 

From the PDF solution: $\det(2(A+I))=120$, so $\det(\text{adj}(2(A+I)))=120^2=14400=2^6\cdot3^2\cdot5^2$, $\alpha=6, \beta=2, \gamma=2$, $\alpha^2+\beta^2+\gamma^2=36+4+4=44$

questions.subject: Mathematics
questions.question_text: Let $S = \{p_1, p_2, \ldots, p_{10}\}$ be the set of first ten prime numbers. Let $A = S\cup P$, where $P$ is the set of all possible products of distinct elements of $S$. Then the number of all ordered pairs $(x,y)$, $x\in S$, $y\in A$, such that $x$ divides $y$, is ______.
questions.solution_text:
For a prime $x = p_i \in S$, we need to count $y \in A$ such that $p_i | y$.

$y$ can be $p_i$ itself (from $S$), or any product of distinct elements from $S$ that includes $p_i$.

Products containing $p_i$: choose remaining factors from the other 9 primes: $2^9$ subsets (each subset gives a valid product, including the empty subset giving $y = p_i$).

So for each $x = p_i$, number of valid $y = 2^9 = 512$.

Total ordered pairs $= 10 \times 512 = 5120$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Energy stored in parallel plate capacitor
questions.question_text: Consider a parallel plate capacitor of area $A$ (of each plate) and separation $d$ between the plates. If $E$ is the electric field and $\varepsilon_0$ is the permittivity of free space between the plates, then the potential energy stored in the capacitor is:
questions.solution_text:
Energy density in electric field $= \dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2$

Volume between plates $= Ad$

Total energy $U = \dfrac{1}{2}\varepsilon_0 E^2 \cdot Ad$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: What is the relative decrease in focal length of a lens for an increase in optical power by $0.1$ D from $2.5$ D? ['D' stands for dioptre]

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Surface tension / excess pressure in bubble
questions.question_text: An air bubble of radius $0.1$ cm lies at a depth of $20$ cm below the free surface of a liquid of density $1000\;\text{kg/m}^3$. If the pressure inside the bubble is $2100\;\text{N/m}^2$ greater than the atmospheric pressure, then the surface tension of the liquid in SI unit is (use $g = 10\;\text{m/s}^2$)
questions.solution_text:
Pressure inside bubble: $P_{in} = P_0 + \rho gh + \dfrac{2T}{R}$

$P_{in} - P_0 = \rho gh + \dfrac{2T}{R} = 2100$

$\rho gh = 1000 \times 10 \times 0.2 = 2000\;\text{N/m}^2$

$\dfrac{2T}{R} = 2100-2000 = 100$

$T = \dfrac{100 \times R}{2} = \dfrac{100 \times 0.001}{2} = 0.05\;\text{N/m}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: For an experimental expression $y = \dfrac{32.3 \times 1125}{27.4}$, where all the digits are significant. Then to report the value of $y$ we should write:
questions.solution_text:
$y = \dfrac{32.3 \times 1125}{27.4} = 1326.186...$

The least number of significant figures among operands: $32.3$ and $27.4$ have 3 significant figures each, $1125$ has 4. Minimum is 3.

Rounding $1326.186$ to 3 significant figures: $1330$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Bohr model / energy levels and wavelengths
questions.question_text: During the transition of electron from state A to state C of a Bohr atom, the wavelength of emitted radiation is $2000$ Å and it becomes $6000$ Å when the electron jumps from state B to state C. Then the wavelength of the radiation emitted during the transition of electrons from state A to state B is:
questions.solution_text:
$E_A - E_C = \dfrac{hc}{2000}$ ...(i), $E_B - E_C = \dfrac{hc}{6000}$ ...(ii)

$E_A - E_B = (E_A-E_C)-(E_B-E_C) = hc\left(\dfrac{1}{2000}-\dfrac{1}{6000}\right) = hc \cdot \dfrac{3-1}{6000} = \dfrac{hc}{3000}$

$\lambda_{AB} = 3000$ Å

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
Consider the following statements:
A. The junction area of solar cell is made very narrow compared to a photo diode.
B. Solar cells are not connected with any external bias.
C. LED is made of lightly doped p-n junction.
D. Increase of forward current results in continuous increase of LED light intensity.
E. LEDs have to be connected in forward bias for emission of light.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text:
A: False — Solar cells have large junction area (to absorb more light).
B: True — Solar cells operate without external bias.
C: False — LED is made of heavily doped p-n junction.
D: False — LED intensity increases up to a limit, beyond which it can be damaged.
E: True — LEDs emit light only in forward bias.

Correct statements: B and E → Option (4)

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The amount of work done to break a big water drop of radius $R$ into $27$ small drops of equal radius is $10$ J. The work done required to break the same big drop into $64$ small drops of equal radius will be:
questions.solution_text:
$W = S \cdot 4\pi R^2(n^{1/3}-1)$ where $n$ = number of drops.

For $n=27$: $W_1 = S\cdot4\pi R^2(3-1) = 2S\cdot4\pi R^2 = 10$ J

For $n=64$: $W_2 = S\cdot4\pi R^2(4-1) = 3S\cdot4\pi R^2$

$\dfrac{W_2}{W_1} = \dfrac{3}{2} \Rightarrow W_2 = 15$ J

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An object of mass $m$ is projected from the origin in a vertical $xy$ plane at an angle $45°$ with the $x$-axis with an initial velocity $v_0$. The magnitude and direction of the angular momentum of the object with respect to origin, when it reaches the maximum height, will be $[g$ is acceleration due to gravity$]$
questions.solution_text:
At $45°$: $v_x = v_0/\sqrt{2}$, $v_y = v_0/\sqrt{2}$.

At max height: $v_y = 0$, $v_x = v_0/\sqrt{2}$, and $H = \dfrac{v_y^2}{2g} = \dfrac{v_0^2}{4g}$, $x = \dfrac{v_0^2}{2g}$ (half range).

$\vec{L} = m\vec{r}\times\vec{v} = m(x\hat{i}+H\hat{j})\times(v_x\hat{i})$

$= m\cdot H\hat{j}\times v_x\hat{i} = mHv_x(\hat{j}\times\hat{i}) = -mHv_x\hat{k}$

$= -m \cdot \dfrac{v_0^2}{4g} \cdot \dfrac{v_0}{\sqrt{2}}\hat{k} = -\dfrac{mv_0^3}{4\sqrt{2}g}\hat{k}$

Magnitude $\dfrac{mv_0^3}{4\sqrt{2}g}$ along negative $z$-axis.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The Young's double slit interference experiment is performed using light consisting of $480$ nm and $600$ nm wavelengths to form interference patterns. The least number of the bright fringes of $480$ nm light that are required for the first coincidence with the bright fringes formed by $600$ nm light is:
questions.solution_text:
Coincidence: $n_1\lambda_1 = n_2\lambda_2$

$n_1 \times 480 = n_2 \times 600$

$\dfrac{n_1}{n_2} = \dfrac{600}{480} = \dfrac{5}{4}$

Minimum: $n_1 = 5$, $n_2 = 4$.

So 5 fringes of 480 nm coincide with 4 fringes of 600 nm.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Banking of roads / coefficient of friction
questions.question_text: A car of mass $m$ moves on a banked road having radius $r$ and banking angle $\theta$. To avoid slipping from the banked road, the maximum permissible speed of the car is $v_0$. The coefficient of friction $\mu$ between the wheels of the car and the banked road is:
questions.solution_text:
For maximum speed on banked road:

$N\sin\theta + f\cos\theta = \dfrac{mv_0^2}{r}$ (centripetal)

$N\cos\theta - f\sin\theta = mg$ (vertical)

$f = \mu N$ at maximum speed.

Dividing: $\dfrac{\sin\theta+\mu\cos\theta}{\cos\theta-\mu\sin\theta} = \dfrac{v_0^2}{rg}$

$rg(\sin\theta+\mu\cos\theta) = v_0^2(\cos\theta-\mu\sin\theta)$

$rg\sin\theta + rg\mu\cos\theta = v_0^2\cos\theta - v_0^2\mu\sin\theta$

$\mu(rg\cos\theta+v_0^2\sin\theta) = v_0^2\cos\theta - rg\sin\theta$

$\mu = \dfrac{v_0^2\cos\theta - rg\sin\theta}{rg\cos\theta+v_0^2\sin\theta} = \dfrac{v_0^2-rg\tan\theta}{rg+v_0^2\tan\theta}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A uniform solid cylinder of mass $m$ and radius $r$ rolls along an inclined rough plane of inclination $45°$. If it starts to roll from rest from the top of the plane then the linear acceleration of the cylinder axis will be:
questions.solution_text:
For rolling without slipping: $a = \dfrac{g\sin\theta}{1+I/(mR^2)}$

For solid cylinder: $I = \dfrac{1}{2}mR^2 \Rightarrow I/(mR^2) = 1/2$

$a = \dfrac{g\sin45°}{1+1/2} = \dfrac{g/\sqrt{2}}{3/2} = \dfrac{2g}{3\sqrt{2}} = \dfrac{\sqrt{2}g}{3}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A thin plano-convex lens made of glass of refractive index $1.5$ is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.2$. When the plane side of the lens is silver coated for complete reflection, the lens immersed in the liquid behaves like a concave mirror of focal length $0.2$ m. The radius of curvature of the curved surface of the lens is:
questions.solution_text:
Equivalent mirror: $\dfrac{1}{f_{eq}} = \dfrac{1}{f_m} + \dfrac{2}{f_l}$ where $f_m = \infty$ (plane mirror).

So $f_{eq} = f_l/2$.

For plano-convex lens in liquid:
$\dfrac{1}{f_l} = \left(\dfrac{n_g}{n_l}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R_1}-\dfrac{1}{R_2}\right) = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.2}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{R}-0\right) = \dfrac{0.3}{1.2}\cdot\dfrac{1}{R} = \dfrac{1}{4R}$

$f_{eq} = f_l/2 = 2R$

$2R = 0.2 \Rightarrow R = 0.1$ m

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A particle is executing simple harmonic motion with time period $2$ s and amplitude $1$ cm. If $D$ and $d$ are the total distance and displacement covered by the particle in $12.5$ s, then $\dfrac{D}{d}$ is:
questions.solution_text:
$T = 2$ s, $A = 1$ cm.

$n = 12.5/2 = 6.25$ cycles.

In each complete cycle, distance $= 4A = 4$ cm.
In 6 complete cycles: $D_1 = 24$ cm.

Extra $0.25$ cycle $= T/4$ starting from extreme: covers $A = 1$ cm.

Total $D = 24+1 = 25$ cm.

For displacement: after 6 complete cycles, particle is at starting position. In extra $T/4$ from extreme, particle is at equilibrium: displacement $= 1$ cm.

$\dfrac{D}{d} = \dfrac{25}{1} = 25$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A satellite is launched into a circular orbit of radius $R$ around the earth. A second satellite is launched into an orbit of radius $1.03R$. The time period of the second satellite is larger than the first one approximately by:
questions.solution_text:
$T^2 \propto R^3 \Rightarrow T \propto R^{3/2}$

$\dfrac{\Delta T}{T} = \dfrac{3}{2}\cdot\dfrac{\Delta R}{R} = \dfrac{3}{2}\times 0.03 = 0.045 = 4.5\%$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Focal length of lenses in different media
questions.question_text: A plano-convex lens having radius of curvature of first surface $2$ cm exhibits focal length of $f_1$ in air. Another plano-convex lens with first surface radius of curvature $3$ cm has focal length of $f_2$ when it is immersed in a liquid of refractive index $1.2$. If both the lenses are made of same glass of refractive index $1.5$, the ratio of $f_1$ and $f_2$ will be:
questions.solution_text:
Lens 1 in air: $\dfrac{1}{f_1} = (1.5-1)\left(\dfrac{1}{2}-0\right) = 0.5\times0.5 = 0.25 \Rightarrow f_1 = 4$ cm

Lens 2 in liquid ($n_l=1.2$): $\dfrac{1}{f_2} = \left(\dfrac{1.5}{1.2}-1\right)\left(\dfrac{1}{3}-0\right) = \dfrac{0.3}{1.2}\times\dfrac{1}{3} = \dfrac{0.3}{3.6} = \dfrac{1}{12} \Rightarrow f_2 = 12$ cm

$f_1:f_2 = 4:12 = 1:3$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: An alternating current is given by $I = I_A\sin\omega t + I_B\cos\omega t$. The r.m.s. current will be:
questions.solution_text:
$I^2 = (I_A\sin\omega t+I_B\cos\omega t)^2 = I_A^2\sin^2\omega t + 2I_AI_B\sin\omega t\cos\omega t + I_B^2\cos^2\omega t$

$\langle I^2\rangle = I_A^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2}+0+I_B^2\cdot\dfrac{1}{2} = \dfrac{I_A^2+I_B^2}{2}$

$I_{rms} = \sqrt{\dfrac{I_A^2+I_B^2}{2}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: de Broglie wavelength in electric field
questions.question_text: An electron of mass $m$ with an initial velocity $\vec{v}=v_0\hat{i}$ ($v_0>0$) enters an electric field $\vec{E}=-E_0\hat{k}$. If the initial de Broglie wavelength is $\lambda_0$, the value after time $t$ would be:
questions.solution_text:
Acceleration $= \dfrac{eE_0}{m}\hat{k}$ (force on electron $= -e\vec{E} = eE_0\hat{k}$)

Velocity at time $t$: $\vec{v} = v_0\hat{i} + \dfrac{eE_0}{m}t\hat{k}$

$|\vec{v}| = \sqrt{v_0^2+\dfrac{e^2E_0^2t^2}{m^2}}$

$\lambda = \dfrac{h}{m|v|} = \dfrac{h}{mv_0\sqrt{1+\dfrac{e^2E_0^2t^2}{m^2v_0^2}}} = \dfrac{\lambda_0}{\sqrt{1+\dfrac{e^2E_0^2t^2}{m^2v_0^2}}}$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
A parallel plate capacitor was made with two rectangular plates, each with a length of $l=3$ cm and breadth of $b=1$ cm. The distance between the plates is $3\;\mu$m. Out of the following, which are the ways to increase the capacitance by a factor of $10$?

A. $l=30$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=1\;\mu$m
B. $l=3$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=30\;\mu$m
C. $l=6$ cm, $b=5$ cm, $d=3\;\mu$m
D. $l=1$ cm, $b=1$ cm, $d=10\;\mu$m
E. $l=5$ cm, $b=2$ cm, $d=1\;\mu$m

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text:
Original $C = \varepsilon_0\dfrac{lb}{d} = \varepsilon_0\dfrac{3\times1}{3} = \varepsilon_0$ units.

Target: $10\varepsilon_0$.

A: $\dfrac{30\times1}{1}=30\varepsilon_0$ ✗

B: $\dfrac{3\times1}{30}=0.1\varepsilon_0$ ✗

C: $\dfrac{6\times5}{3}=10\varepsilon_0$ ✓

D: $\dfrac{1\times1}{10}=0.1\varepsilon_0$ ✗

E: $\dfrac{5\times2}{1}=10\varepsilon_0$ ✓

Answer: C and E only

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A force $F = \alpha + \beta x^2$ acts on an object in the $x$-direction. The work done by the force is $5$ J when the object is displaced by $1$ m. If the constant $\alpha = 1$ N then $\beta$ will be
questions.solution_text:
$W = \displaystyle\int_0^1 F\,dx = \int_0^1(\alpha+\beta x^2)\,dx = \left[\alpha x+\dfrac{\beta x^3}{3}\right]_0^1 = \alpha+\dfrac{\beta}{3} = 5$

With $\alpha=1$: $1+\dfrac{\beta}{3}=5 \Rightarrow \dfrac{\beta}{3}=4 \Rightarrow \beta=12\;\text{N/m}^2$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text:
An ideal gas goes from an initial state to final state. During the process, the pressure of gas increases linearly with temperature.

A. The work done by gas during the process is zero.
B. The heat added to gas is different from change in its internal energy.
C. The volume of the gas is increased.
D. The internal energy of the gas is increased.
E. The process is isochoric (constant volume process)

Choose the **correct** answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text:
$P \propto T \Rightarrow P/T = $ constant $\Rightarrow$ from ideal gas law $PV=nRT$: $V=nR\cdot(T/P)=$ const.

So process is isochoric (constant volume), work done $=0$, $Q=\Delta U>0$ (temperature increases).

A: True (W=0 for isochoric)
B: False ($Q = \Delta U$ for isochoric)
C: False (volume is constant)
D: True (temperature increases, so internal energy increases)
E: True

Correct: A, D, E

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: A square loop of sides $a=1$ m is held normally in front of a point charge $q=1$ C. The flux of the electric field through the shaded region is $\dfrac{5}{p}\times\dfrac{1}{\varepsilon_0}\;\dfrac{\text{Nm}^2}{\text{C}}$, where the value of $p$ is ____.
questions.solution_text:
Total flux through the square face of a cube (charge at corner): $\dfrac{q}{\varepsilon_0}\times\dfrac{1}{6} = \dfrac{q}{6\varepsilon_0}$.

Divide the square into 8 equal parts. The shaded region corresponds to $5/8$ of the square.

Flux through shaded region $= \dfrac{5}{8}\times\dfrac{1}{6\varepsilon_0} = \dfrac{5}{48\varepsilon_0}$

So $p = 48$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.question_text: The least count of a screw gauge is $0.01$ mm. If the pitch is increased by $75\%$ and number of divisions on the circular scale is reduced by $50\%$, the new least count will be ______$\times10^{-3}$ mm.
questions.solution_text:
LC $= \dfrac{\text{Pitch}}{N} = 0.01$ mm.

New pitch $= P\times1.75$, New $N = 0.5N$

New LC $= \dfrac{1.75P}{0.5N} = 3.5\times\dfrac{P}{N} = 3.5\times0.01 = 0.035$ mm $= 35\times10^{-3}$ mm

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Resistance of wire bent into triangle
questions.question_text: A wire of resistance $9\;\Omega$ is bent to form an equilateral triangle. Then the equivalent resistance across any two vertices will be ____$\;\Omega$.
questions.solution_text:
Each side of equilateral triangle has resistance $3\;\Omega$.

Across two vertices: one path has resistance $3\;\Omega$, other path has $3+3=6\;\Omega$.

$R_{eq} = \dfrac{3\times6}{3+6} = \dfrac{18}{9} = 2\;\Omega$

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Magnetic field at centre of square loop
questions.question_text: A current of $5$ A exists in a square loop of side $\dfrac{1}{\sqrt{2}}$ m. Then the magnitude of the magnetic field $B$ at the centre of the square loop will be $p\times10^{-6}$ T. where value of $p$ is ______. [Take $\mu_0 = 4\pi\times10^{-7}$ T mA$^{-1}$]
questions.solution_text:
For square loop, side $a=1/\sqrt{2}$ m, distance from centre to side $d = a/2 = 1/(2\sqrt{2})$ m.

Field due to one side at centre:
$B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}(\sin45°+\sin45°) = \dfrac{10^{-7}\times5}{1/(2\sqrt{2})}\times\sqrt{2} = 10^{-7}\times5\times2\sqrt{2}\times\sqrt{2} = 10^{-7}\times5\times4$... 

Using formula: $B_1 = \dfrac{\mu_0 i}{4\pi d}\cdot2\sin45° = \dfrac{10^{-7}\times5}{1/(2\sqrt{2})}\times\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = 10^{-7}\times5\times2\sqrt{2}\times\dfrac{2}{\sqrt{2}} = 10^{-7}\times20 = 2\times10^{-6}$ T per side.

Total (4 sides): $B = 4\times2\times10^{-6} = 8\times10^{-6}$ T, so $p=8$.

questions.subject: Physics
questions.topic: Heat and internal energy of monoatomic gas
questions.question_text: The temperature of $1$ mole of an ideal monoatomic gas is increased by $50°$C at constant pressure. The total heat added and change in internal energy are $E_1$ and $E_2$, respectively. If $\dfrac{E_1}{E_2}=\dfrac{x}{9}$ then the value of $x$ is ______.
questions.solution_text:
Monoatomic ideal gas: $C_V = \dfrac{3}{2}R$, $C_P = \dfrac{5}{2}R$, $\gamma = \dfrac{C_P}{C_V} = \dfrac{5}{3}$

$E_1 = nC_P\Delta T$, $E_2 = nC_V\Delta T$

$\dfrac{E_1}{E_2} = \dfrac{C_P}{C_V} = \gamma = \dfrac{5}{3} = \dfrac{x}{9}$

$x = 9\times\dfrac{5}{3} = 15$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Standard cell potential from standard electrode potentials
questions.question_text:
For the given cell
$\text{Fe}^{2+}(\text{eq})+\text{Ag}^+(\text{aq})\to\text{Fe}^{3+}(\text{aq})+\text{Ag(s)}$
The standard cell potential of the above reaction is given:
$\text{Ag}^+ + e^- \to \text{Ag}$, $E^0 = x$ V
$\text{Fe}^{2+}+2e^-\to\text{Fe}$, $E^0 = y$ V
$\text{Fe}^{3+}+3e^-\to\text{Fe}$, $E^0 = z$ V
questions.solution_text:
Using Hess's law with Gibbs energy:
$\Delta G_3^0 = \Delta G_1^0 + \Delta G_2^0$ where Fe→Fe$^{2+}$→Fe$^{3+}$

$-3Fz = -2Fy + \Delta G_2^0 \Rightarrow \Delta G_2^0 = 2Fy-3Fz$

$E_{\text{Fe}^{2+}/\text{Fe}^{3+}}^0 = -\dfrac{\Delta G_2^0}{F} = 2y-3z$... actually:

For $\text{Fe}^{2+}\to\text{Fe}^{3+}+e^-$: $\Delta G = -(2y-3z)F$

$E_{\text{Fe}^{3+}/\text{Fe}^{2+}}^0 = 3z-2y$

$E_{\text{cell}}^0 = E_{\text{cathode}}^0 - E_{\text{anode}}^0 = x-(3z-2y) = x+2y-3z$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Following are the four molecules 'P', 'Q', 'R' and 'S' (structures: P is dihydropyran, Q is 2H-pyran, R is methylenecyclohexane type, S is a trimethylcyclohexene type). Which one among the four molecules will react with $\text{H-Br}_{(aq)}$ at the fastest rate?
questions.solution_text:
HBr addition to alkenes follows electrophilic addition mechanism. The rate-determining step involves carbocation formation.

Among P, Q, R, S: compound Q (2H-pyran type with oxygen adjacent to double bond) forms the most stable carbocation intermediate because the oxygen lone pair provides resonance stabilization to the adjacent carbocation (oxocarbenium ion).

This makes Q react fastest with HBr.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: One mole of the octahedral complex compound $\text{Co(NH}_3)_3\text{Cl}_3$ gives $3$ moles of ions on dissolution in water. One mole of the same complex reacts with excess of $\text{AgNO}_3$ solution to yield two moles of $\text{AgCl}_{(s)}$. The structure of the complex is:
questions.solution_text:
$[\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]\text{Cl}_2 \to [\text{Co(NH}_3)_5\text{Cl}]^{2+}(\text{aq}) + 2\text{Cl}^-(\text{aq})$ → 3 ions ✓

With AgNO$_3$: 2 Cl$^-$ ions (outside coordination sphere) precipitate as 2 AgCl ✓

This is option (1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Which one of the carbocations from the following is most stable? (Options show allylic carbocations with different substituents near oxygen-containing groups)
questions.solution_text:
Carbocation stability is enhanced by +I, +M effects and hyperconjugation.

Option (2): $^+\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-OCH}_3$ — the carbocation is in conjugation with the vinyl ether system. The $-\text{OCH}_3$ group directly attached to double bond provides strong +M (mesomeric) effect through resonance: $^+\text{CH}_2\text{-CH=CH-}\overset{..}{\text{O}}\text{-CH}_3 \leftrightarrow \text{CH}_2\text{=CH-CH=}\overset{+}{\text{O}}\text{-CH}_3$

This makes option (2) the most stable carbocation.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Molecular orbital formation from atomic orbitals
questions.question_text:
Which of the following linear combination of atomic orbitals will lead to formation of molecular orbitals in homonuclear diatomic molecules [internuclear axis in $z$-direction]?
A. $2p_z$ and $2p_x$
B. $2s$ and $2p_x$
C. $3d_{xy}$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$
D. $2s$ and $2p_z$
E. $2p_z$ and $3d_{x^2-y^2}$
questions.solution_text:
For MO formation, orbitals must have: (1) similar energies, (2) same symmetry about the internuclear ($z$) axis, (3) significant overlap.

A: $2p_z$ (sigma symmetry) + $2p_x$ (pi symmetry) → different symmetries, no MO.
B: $2s$ (sigma) + $2p_x$ (pi symmetry about $z$) → different symmetries, no MO.
C: $3d_{xy}$ + $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ → different symmetry about $z$, no MO.
D: $2s$ (sigma/spherical) + $2p_z$ (sigma) → same symmetry ($\sigma$), can combine → MO formed ✓
E: $2p_z$ (sigma) + $3d_{x^2-y^2}$ (delta symmetry) → different symmetry, no MO.

Only D forms MOs.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following ions is the strongest oxidizing agent?
(Atomic Number of Ce$=58$, Eu$=63$, Tb$=65$, Lu$=71$)
questions.solution_text:
Strongest oxidizing agent = species most easily reduced (highest tendency to gain electrons).

$\text{Tb}^{4+}$ has an empty $f$-orbital configuration and strongly prefers to be reduced to $\text{Tb}^{3+}$ (stable $4f^8$ configuration, half-filled +1). This makes $\text{Tb}^{4+}$ the strongest oxidizing agent among the options.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: $K_{sp}$ for $\text{Cr(OH)}_3$ is $1.6\times10^{-30}$. What is the molar solubility of this salt in water?
questions.solution_text:
$\text{Cr(OH)}_3 \rightleftharpoons \text{Cr}^{3+} + 3\text{OH}^-$

If solubility $= s$: $[\text{Cr}^{3+}]=s$, $[\text{OH}^-]=3s$

$K_{sp} = s\cdot(3s)^3 = 27s^4 = 1.6\times10^{-30}$

$s^4 = \dfrac{1.6\times10^{-30}}{27}$

$s = \left(\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-30}}{27}\right)^{1/4} = 4\sqrt{\dfrac{1.6\times10^{-30}}{27}}$ (fourth root)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Let us consider an endothermic reaction which is non-spontaneous at the freezing point of water. However, the reaction is spontaneous at boiling point of water. Choose the correct option.
questions.solution_text:
$\Delta G = \Delta H - T\Delta S$

Endothermic: $\Delta H > 0$.
Non-spontaneous at low $T$: $\Delta G > 0$ at $T=273$ K.
Spontaneous at high $T$: $\Delta G < 0$ at $T=373$ K.

For $\Delta G$ to decrease with increasing $T$: $-T\Delta S$ must decrease, so $\Delta S > 0$.

With $\Delta H>0$ and $\Delta S>0$: $\Delta G=\Delta H-T\Delta S$ is positive at low $T$ (where $T\Delta S<\Delta H$) and negative at high $T$ (where $T\Delta S>\Delta H$). This matches the observations.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
**Statement I:** Dumas method is used for estimation of 'Nitrogen' in an organic compound.
**Statement II:** Dumas method involves the formation of ammonium sulphate by heating the organic compound with conc $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: Both Statement I and Statement II are true
Statement I is false but Statement II is true
Both Statement I and Statement II are false
Statement I is true but Statement II is false

questions.solution_text:
Statement I: TRUE — Dumas method estimates nitrogen in organic compounds by converting it to $N_2$ gas.

Statement II: FALSE — Dumas method involves heating with CuO (not conc $H_2SO_4$) which gives $N_2$ gas measured volumetrically. It is Kjeldahl's method that uses $H_2SO_4$ and forms ammonium sulphate.

Answer: Statement I true, II false → Option (4)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following Statements are NOT true about the periodic table?
A. The properties of elements are function of atomic weights.
B. The properties of elements are function of atomic numbers.
C. Elements having similar outer electronic configuration are arranged in same period.
D. An element's location reflects the quantum numbers of the last filled orbital.
E. The number of elements in a period is same as the number of atomic orbitals available in energy level that is being filled.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text:
A: FALSE — properties are function of atomic numbers (Mendeleev initially used atomic weight, but modern periodic law uses atomic number).
B: TRUE — Moseley's periodic law.
C: FALSE — similar outer electronic configuration → same group, not same period.
D: TRUE — position reflects quantum numbers of valence electrons.
E: FALSE — number of elements ≠ number of atomic orbitals in that energy level (e.g., period 4 has 18 elements, but 4s,3d,4p orbitals give different count).

Statements NOT true: A, C, E → Option (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
The carbohydrates 'Ribose' present in DNA, is
A. A pentose sugar
B. present in pyranose form
C. in 'D' configuration
D. a reducing sugar, when free
E. in $\alpha$-anomeric form

Choose the correct answer from the options given below:
questions.solution_text:
The sugar in DNA is $\beta$-2-Deoxy-D-Ribose.

A: TRUE — it is a pentose (5-carbon) sugar.
B: FALSE — it is in furanose form (5-membered ring), not pyranose.
C: TRUE — it is D-configuration.
D: TRUE — when free (not in nucleoside), it is a reducing sugar.
E: FALSE — in DNA, it is in $\beta$-anomeric form, not $\alpha$.

Correct: A, C, D → Option (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Preparation of potassium permanganate from $\text{MnO}_2$ involves two step process in which the $1^{\text{st}}$ step is a reaction with KOH and KNO$_3$ to produce
questions.solution_text:
$\text{MnO}_2 \xrightarrow{\text{KOH/KNO}_3, \Delta} \text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$ (potassium manganate, step 1)

Then $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4 \xrightarrow{\text{electrolytic oxidation or Cl}_2} \text{KMnO}_4$ (step 2)

First product is $\text{K}_2\text{MnO}_4$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: The large difference between the melting and boiling points of oxygen and sulphur may be explained on the basis of
questions.solution_text:
Oxygen exists as $\text{O}_2$ (atomicity = 2) while sulphur exists as $\text{S}_8$ (atomicity = 8).

Higher atomicity means larger molecular mass and stronger London dispersion forces, leading to significantly higher melting and boiling points for sulphur compared to oxygen.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Pressure at equilibrium from degree of dissociation
questions.question_text: For a reaction, $\text{N}_2\text{O}_{5(g)} \to 2\text{NO}_{2(g)} + \dfrac{1}{2}\text{O}_{2(g)}$ in a constant volume container, no products were present initially. The final pressure of the system when $50\%$ of reaction gets completed is
questions.solution_text:
At $t=0$: $P_0$ moles of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$.

At 50% completion, $x = P_0/2$ decomposed:
$\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$: $P_0-x = P_0/2$
$\text{NO}_2$: $2x = P_0$
$\text{O}_2$: $x/2 = P_0/4$

$P_{\text{total}} = P_0/2 + P_0 + P_0/4 = P_0(2+4+1)/4 = \dfrac{7P_0}{4}$

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following arrangements with respect to their reactivity in nucleophilic addition reaction is correct?
(Compounds: benzaldehyde, acetophenone, p-nitrobenzaldehyde, p-tolualdehyde)
questions.solution_text:
Nucleophilic addition reactivity decreases with steric crowding and increases with electron-withdrawing groups at carbonyl carbon.

Acetophenone: bulky methyl + phenyl on carbonyl → least reactive.
p-Tolualdehyde: aldehyde with electron-donating $-\text{CH}_3$ group → less reactive than benzaldehyde.
Benzaldehyde: simple aldehyde.
p-Nitrobenzaldehyde: electron-withdrawing $-\text{NO}_2$ activates carbonyl → most reactive.

Order: acetophenone < p-tolualdehyde < benzaldehyde < p-nitrobenzaldehyde

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Aman has been asked to synthesise the molecule $x$ (a cyclopentene derivative with a side chain $-\text{C(=O)-CH}_3$). He performs ozonolysis on a cyclic alkene to get a dicarbonyl compound followed by aldol condensation. Predict the suitable alkene that can lead to the formation of 'x'.
questions.solution_text:
Target molecule $x$ is 2-(1-oxoethyl)cyclopent-2-en-1-one type — a cyclopentenone with acetyl group.

Ozonolysis of 1-methylcyclohexene cleaves the double bond to give a 7-carbon ketoaldehyde: $\text{CH}_3\text{-C(=O)-(CH}_2)_4\text{-CHO}$ (a 7-oxoheptanal).

Intramolecular aldol condensation of this dialdehyde/ketoaldehyde gives a 5-membered ring (cyclopentenone derivative) with loss of water, forming compound $x$.

So the alkene is 1-methylcyclohexene (option 1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Depression in freezing point / VP-T graph
questions.question_text: Consider the given plots of vapour pressure (VP) vs temperature (T/K). Which amongst the following options is the correct graphical representation showing $\Delta T_f$, depression in the freezing point of solvent in a solution?
questions.solution_text:
On freezing, $T_f < T_f^0$ (freezing point of solution is lower than pure solvent).

The correct graph must show:
1. VP of liquid solvent curve above the VP of solution curve.
2. VP of frozen solution below both.
3. The intersection of 'frozen solution' VP curve with 'solution' VP curve occurs at $T_f$ (lower), while intersection with 'liquid solvent' occurs at $T_f^0$ (higher).
4. $\Delta T_f = T_f^0 - T_f$ shown on temperature axis.

Option (3) correctly shows this arrangement with $T_f < T_f^0$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Which of the following statement is true with respect to $\text{H}_2\text{O}$, $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{CH}_4$?
A. The central atoms of all the molecules are $sp^3$ hybridized.
B. The H–O–H, H–N–H and H–C–H angles in the above molecules are $104.5°$, $107.5°$ and $109.5°$ respectively.
C. The increasing order of dipole moment is $\text{CH}_4 < \text{NH}_3 < \text{H}_2\text{O}$.
D. Both $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ are Lewis acids and $\text{CH}_4$ is a Lewis base.
E. A solution of $\text{NH}_3$ in $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is basic. In this solution $\text{NH}_3$ and $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ act as Lowry-Bronsted acid and base respectively.
Choose the correct answer from the options given below:

options.text: A, B, C and E only

questions.solution_text:
A: TRUE — all three have $sp^3$ hybridization (O,N,C).
B: TRUE — bond angles as stated.
C: TRUE — $\text{CH}_4$ is symmetric (dipole = 0) < $\text{NH}_3$ < $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ (highest due to two lone pairs).
D: FALSE — $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ and $\text{NH}_3$ are Lewis bases (electron donors), not Lewis acids.
E: FALSE — In $\text{NH}_3/\text{H}_2\text{O}$: $\text{NH}_3$ is the Brønsted base (accepts proton), $\text{H}_2\text{O}$ is the Brønsted acid (donates proton), not the reverse.

Correct: A, B, C → Option (1)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text:
Given below are two statements:
**Statement-I:** The conversion $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\xrightarrow{\text{HO}^-}\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{OH}+\text{Cl}^-$ proceeds well in the less polar medium.
**Statement-II:** The conversion $\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{Cl}\xrightarrow{R_3N}\text{CH}_3\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{CH}_2\text{NR}_3^+\text{Cl}^-$ proceeds well in the more polar medium.
In the light of the above statements, choose the correct answer from the options given below.

options.text: Both statement I and statement II are true
Both statement I and statement II are false
Statement I is false but statement II is true
Statement I is true but statement II is false

questions.solution_text:
Statement I: SN2 reaction with HO$^-$ (charged reactant → neutral-like transition state with distributed charge). High charge density reactant → less polar solvent favors the reaction (transition state has lower charge density than reactant). TRUE.

Statement II: SN2 with $R_3N$ (neutral reactant → charged transition state with higher charge density). More polar solvent stabilizes the higher-charge transition state, facilitating the reaction. TRUE.

Both statements are correct → Option (1).

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.topic: Reaction sequence: Markovnikov addition, HCN, hydrogenation
questions.question_text:
The product (A) formed in the following reaction sequence is:
$\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH}\xrightarrow{(i)\,\text{Hg}^{2+},\,\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}\xrightarrow{(ii)\,\text{HCN}}\xrightarrow{(iii)\,\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}}$ (A)
questions.solution_text:
Step 1: $\text{CH}_3\text{-C}\equiv\text{CH}\xrightarrow{\text{Hg}^{2+}/\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4}\text{CH}_3\text{-C(=O)-CH}_3$ (Markovnikov hydration gives acetone)

Step 2: Acetone $+$ HCN $\to \text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)(CN)-CH}_3$ (cyanohydrin)

Step 3: $\xrightarrow{\text{H}_2/\text{Ni}}\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)(CH}_2\text{NH}_2)\text{-CH}_3$ (CN reduced to $\text{CH}_2\text{NH}_2$, no change in OH)

Product: $\text{CH}_3\text{-C(OH)(CH}_2\text{NH}_2)\text{-CH}_3$ = 2-methyl-2-hydroxy-1-aminopropane → Option (2)

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: $37.8$ g $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ was taken in a $1$ L reaction vessel and allowed to undergo the following reaction at $500$ K: $2\text{N}_2\text{O}_{5(g)} \to 2\text{N}_2\text{O}_{4(g)} + \text{O}_{2(g)}$. The total pressure at equilibrium was found to be $18.65$ bar. Then $K_p = $ ______ $\times10^{-2}$ [nearest integer]. Assume $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5$ to behave ideally. Given: $R = 0.082$ bar L mol$^{-1}$ K$^{-1}$
questions.solution_text:
Moles of $\text{N}_2\text{O}_5 = 37.8/108 = 0.35$ mol.

Initial pressure: $P_0 = nRT/V = 0.35\times0.082\times500 = 14.35$ bar.

$2\text{N}_2\text{O}_5\to2\text{N}_2\text{O}_4+\text{O}_2$
Initial: $14.35$, 0, 0.
At equil: $14.35-2P$, $2P$, $P$.

$P_{\text{total}} = 14.35+P = 18.65 \Rightarrow P = 4.3$ bar.

$P_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_5}=5.75$ bar, $P_{\text{N}_2\text{O}_4}=8.6$ bar, $P_{\text{O}_2}=4.3$ bar.

$K_p = \dfrac{(8.6)^2\times4.3}{(5.75)^2} = \dfrac{73.96\times4.3}{33.0625} = \dfrac{318.028}{33.0625} \approx 9.619$

$K_p = 9.619 \approx 962\times10^{-2}$, so answer $= 962$.

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Standard entropies of $X_2$, $Y_2$ and $XY_5$ are $70$, $50$ and $110$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$ respectively. The temperature in Kelvin at which the reaction $\dfrac{1}{2}X_2+\dfrac{5}{2}Y_2\to XY_5$, $\Delta H^- = -35$ kJ mol$^{-1}$ will be at equilibrium is ______ (Nearest integer)
questions.solution_text:
$\Delta S_{rxn}^0 = S(XY_5)-\dfrac{1}{2}S(X_2)-\dfrac{5}{2}S(Y_2) = 110-\dfrac{1}{2}(70)-\dfrac{5}{2}(50) = 110-35-125 = -50$ J K$^{-1}$ mol$^{-1}$

At equilibrium: $\Delta G^0 = 0 \Rightarrow \Delta H^0 = T\Delta S^0$

$T = \dfrac{\Delta H^0}{\Delta S^0} = \dfrac{-35000}{-50} = 700$ K

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: $X$ g of benzoic acid on reaction with aq. $\text{NaHCO}_3$ release $\text{CO}_2$ that occupied $11.2$ L volume at STP. $X$ is ______ g.
questions.solution_text:
$\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH}+\text{NaHCO}_3\to\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COONa}+\text{H}_2\text{O}+\text{CO}_2$

Moles of $\text{CO}_2 = \dfrac{11.2}{22.4} = 0.5$ mol

Moles of $\text{C}_6\text{H}_5\text{COOH} = 0.5$ mol

Mass $= 0.5\times122 = 61$ g

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Among the following cations, the number of cations which will give characteristic precipitate in their identification tests with $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ is: $\text{Cu}^{2+}$, $\text{Fe}^{3+}$, $\text{Ba}^{2+}$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{NH}_4^+$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$, $\text{Zn}^{2+}$
questions.solution_text:
$\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ (potassium ferrocyanide) gives characteristic precipitates with:

$\text{Cu}^{2+}$: chocolate brown precipitate of $\text{Cu}_2[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$ ✓
$\text{Fe}^{3+}$: dark blue precipitate (Prussian blue) $\text{Fe}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_3$ ✓
$\text{Zn}^{2+}$: white precipitate of $\text{K}_2\text{Zn}_3[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]_2$ ✓

$\text{Ba}^{2+}$, $\text{Ca}^{2+}$, $\text{NH}_4^+$, $\text{Mg}^{2+}$: no characteristic precipitate with $\text{K}_4[\text{Fe(CN)}_6]$.

Answer: 3

questions.subject: Chemistry
questions.question_text: Consider the following reaction occurring in the blast furnace: $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_{4(s)}+4\text{CO}_{(g)}\to 3\text{Fe}_{(l)}+4\text{CO}_{2(g)}$. '$x$' kg of iron is produced when $2.32\times10^3$ kg $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$ and $2.8\times10^2$ kg CO are brought together in the furnace. The value of '$x$' is ______ (nearest integer). Given: Molar mass of $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4=232$ g mol$^{-1}$, CO$=28$ g mol$^{-1}$, Fe$=56$ g mol$^{-1}$
questions.solution_text:
Moles of $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4 = \dfrac{2.32\times10^6}{232} = 10000$ mol

Moles of CO $= \dfrac{2.8\times10^5}{28} = 10000$ mol

Reaction requires 4 mol CO per mol $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$. For 10000 mol $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$, need 40000 mol CO, but only 10000 available.

CO is limiting reagent: $10000$ mol CO reacts with $10000/4=2500$ mol $\text{Fe}_3\text{O}_4$.

Moles of Fe produced $= 3\times\dfrac{10000}{4} = 7500$ mol.

Mass of Fe $= \dfrac{7500\times56}{1000} = 420$ kg.
